summary: Module 2 BREAK: The Conflicting Assumption. I ran Task 2 (team membership + role-based permissions API) against an AI agent WITHOUT giving it Task 1's actual output as context -- the prompt was written from my ORIGINAL PLAN for what Task 1 would produce. Conflict found: (1) My Task 2 prompt said 'the owner is teams.owner_id' -- but Task 1 actually created Team.created_by, so teams.owner_id DOES NOT EXIST. (2) My Task 2 prompt explicitly instructed 'do not add a members join table; model membership on the teams table via owner_id' -- but Task 1 actually created the team_members join table with a role column (admin/member/viewer). So my prompt assumed the exact opposite data model from what Task 1 built: single-owner flat model vs many-to-many join-table model. The agent DID NOT crash: it silently read the real models and adapted -- used created_by as owner (exposed as owner_id in the response schema) and used the existing team_members table despite my instruction to avoid it. The code compiles and all endpoints work live (201 create, 201 add member, 200 list, 200 update role, 204 delete), 76 tests green. But that silent adaptation IS the failure signal: the agent diverged from my explicit prompt instruction ('no join table') to match reality -- a divergence a reviewer must catch, because it means my prompt and the codebase disagree. Root cause: decomposition bug, not AI bug -- Task 2's prompt relied on the original plan's schema, not on Task 1's actual output (created_by + team_members + role). The conflict is in the DATA MODEL (owner_id vs created_by, flat vs join table), not the API contract. Interface contract lesson: each task prompt after Task 1 MUST embed the previous task's actual output (exact column names, table names) so the AI does not have to guess or silently override instructions. Where does Task 2 reference something Task 1 didn't create? Nothing in the code references owner_id as a column -- the agent mapped it to created_by -- but the PROMPT referenced a nonexistent owner_id column and a nonexistent flat model. If a literal-minded agent had followed the prompt, the code would not compile.
evidence: Task 2 prompt specified teams.owner_id + no join table -- both contradicted by Task 1's actual schema
Agent silently adapted: used created_by as owner, used existing team_members, deviated from 'no join table' instruction
Live check: POST /teams 201, POST members 201, GET members 200, PATCH role 200, DELETE member 204
Root cause: decomposition bug -- prompt written from original plan, not Task 1 output; conflict in data model
